subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In which month and year did Hitler become Chancellor of Germany?
questions.explain: Hitler was appointed Chancellor on 30 January 1933 by President Hindenburg, who hoped to control him.

questions.q: What did many Germans call the politicians who signed the armistice in November 1918?
questions.explain: Many Germans branded the signatories the 'November Criminals', linked to the false 'stab-in-the-back' myth that the army had been betrayed.

questions.q: Which youth opposition group enjoyed banned swing music and rejected Nazi conformity?
questions.explain: The Swing Youth defied Nazi culture by listening to banned jazz and swing music and adopting Western styles.

questions.q: Which country occupied the Ruhr in 1923 when Germany failed to pay reparations?
questions.explain: French and Belgian troops occupied the Ruhr in January 1923 to seize goods in lieu of unpaid reparations.

questions.q: In which year did hyperinflation peak in Germany following the French occupation of the Ruhr?
questions.explain: Hyperinflation reached its peak in 1923, when the mark became almost worthless and prices rose by the hour.

questions.q: Which territory did the Treaty of Versailles force Germany to give to France?
questions.explain: Alsace-Lorraine, taken by Germany in 1871, was returned to France under the Treaty of Versailles.

questions.q: Where did Hitler attempt his failed putsch in November 1923?
questions.explain: The Munich (Beer Hall) Putsch of November 1923 failed, and Hitler was imprisoned, where he wrote Mein Kampf.

questions.q: What was Hitler's official title after he combined Chancellor and President in August 1934?
questions.explain: After Hindenburg's death in August 1934, Hitler merged the offices and became 'Fuhrer', supreme leader of Germany.

questions.q: How much was Germany's reparations bill finally set at in 1921?
questions.explain: In 1921 the reparations were fixed at £6.6 billion, a sum the struggling Weimar economy found crushing.

questions.q: The Nuremberg Laws, which stripped Jews of citizenship and banned intermarriage, were introduced in which year?
questions.explain: The Nuremberg Laws of 1935 deprived Jews of German citizenship and forbade marriage between Jews and non-Jews.

questions.q: What was the name of the failed left-wing communist uprising in Berlin in January 1919?
questions.explain: The Spartacist Revolt of January 1919, led by Karl Liebknecht and Rosa Luxemburg, was crushed by the Freikorps.

questions.q: Which two students led the White Rose resistance group and were executed in 1943?
questions.explain: Hans and Sophie Scholl led the White Rose group, distributing anti-Nazi leaflets in Munich before their execution in 1943.

questions.q: In the July 1932 Reichstag elections, the Nazis became what?
questions.explain: In July 1932 the Nazis won 230 seats, becoming the largest party in the Reichstag though without an overall majority.

questions.q: The 1942 Wannsee Conference is associated with planning what?
questions.explain: At the Wannsee Conference in January 1942, Nazi officials coordinated the 'Final Solution', the systematic murder of Europe's Jews.

questions.q: Who was the first President of the Weimar Republic, elected in 1919?
questions.explain: Friedrich Ebert, leader of the SPD, became the Weimar Republic's first President in 1919 and served until his death in 1925.

questions.q: What was the Nazi-controlled labour organisation that replaced trade unions after 1933 called?
questions.explain: The German Labour Front (DAF), led by Robert Ley, replaced banned trade unions and controlled German workers.

questions.q: The Wall Street Crash, which devastated Germany, occurred in which year?
questions.explain: The Wall Street Crash of October 1929 led American banks to recall loans, plunging Germany into the Depression.

questions.q: Who was the Nazi Minister of Propaganda?
questions.explain: Joseph Goebbels controlled the press, radio, film and rallies to spread Nazi ideology throughout Germany.

questions.q: What was the Nazi leisure programme offering workers cheap holidays and outings called?
questions.explain: 'Strength Through Joy' (Kraft durch Freude) provided subsidised holidays and entertainment to keep workers loyal.

questions.q: What voting system did the 1919 Weimar Constitution use?
options: Single transferable vote for the president only
questions.explain: Proportional representation gave seats in proportion to votes, producing many small parties and unstable coalition governments.

questions.q: Which 1920 right-wing attempt to seize power in Berlin was defeated by a workers' general strike?
options: The Night of the Long Knives
questions.explain: The Kapp Putsch of March 1920 collapsed when Berlin workers staged a general strike that paralysed the capital.

questions.q: What were the November 1938 anti-Jewish pogroms known as?
questions.explain: Kristallnacht ('Night of Broken Glass') in November 1938 saw synagogues and Jewish businesses attacked across Germany.
